issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be rejected for limitation only when, on reading the plaint as a whole, the limitation bar is apparent on its face.
material_facts: The defendants applied to reject the plaint on limitation grounds.

The plaint alleged that advertisements indicating an intended transfer appeared and that an attempt was made to dispossess the plaintiffs in 2010; it identified that attempted dispossession as the cause of action.
The High Court relied on an earlier paragraph of the plaint and did not consider the plaint as a whole.
issues.conclusion: The plaint could not be rejected as facially barred by limitation. The High Court’s order was set aside and the trial court’s refusal to reject the plaint was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a plaint can be rejected for limitation only if the bar is apparent on its face. The court must read the plaint as a whole, rather than isolating selected lines or passages. The Court applied Ram Prakash Gupta v. Rajiv Kumar Gupta, (2007) 10 SCC 59, which states that the whole plaint must be considered when deciding an application under that rule.

rule.if: plaint_rejection_application and limitation_is_basis and plaint_as_a_whole_alleges_a_later_cause_of_action and limitation_bar_not_apparent_on_face

predicates.plaint_rejection_application: A defendant applies to have a plaint rejected before trial.
predicates.limitation_is_basis: The defendant relies on limitation as a ground for rejecting the plaint.
predicates.plaint_as_a_whole_alleges_a_later_cause_: The plaintiffs’ allegations, read together, identify a later event as giving rise to the cause of action.
predicates.limitation_bar_not_apparent_on_face: The allegations in the plaint do not establish, on their face, that the claim is out of time.

issues.definition: When a defendant seeks rejection before trial on limitation grounds, and the plaint as a whole alleges a later cause of action without showing a limitation bar on its face, the plaint is not rejected for limitation.

issues.legal_issue: A plaint seeking interconnected reliefs, including an injunction based on alleged possession under an agreement, cannot be rejected at the threshold merely because the requested declaration under part performance may not be maintainable; entitlement to relief is for trial.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought a declaration and confirmation of possession based on an agreement, specific performance of that agreement, and a permanent injunction.
They alleged that they were in possession under the agreement, had developed the property, had remained in possession for more than twelve years, and paid municipal taxes.
They alleged that the cause of action for the injunction arose when their possession was sought to be disturbed.
The High Court rejected the plaint on the basis that a declaration under the part-performance provision would not be maintainable against the owner.
issues.conclusion: The maintainability of the claimed relief under the part-performance provision was to be considered at trial; it did not justify rejecting the plaint at this stage. The interconnected reliefs could not be rejected partially, and the plaint was restored for trial.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act. Where the plaint also seeks an injunction and alleges possession under an agreement, with the cause of action for the injunction arising when possession is disturbed, the suit cannot be treated as barred on the stated basis at the rejection stage. A plaint cannot be rejected partially, and whether the plaintiffs ultimately qualify for relief under Section 53A must be decided at trial. The Court distinguished the High Court’s reliance on Delhi Motor Company v. U.A. Basrurkar, AIR 1968 SC 794, because the pleadings included the injunction claim and related allegations of possession.

rule.if: plaint_rejection_application and claim_includes_declaration_based_on_part_performance and claim_includes_injunction_based_on_possession and plaintiffs_allege_possession_under_agreement and reliefs_are_interconnected

predicates.plaint_rejection_application: A defendant applies to have a plaint rejected before trial.
predicates.claim_includes_declaration_based_on_part: The plaintiffs seek a declaration based on their alleged performance of an agreement.
predicates.claim_includes_injunction_based_on_posse: The plaintiffs also seek an injunction to protect their alleged possession.
predicates.plaintiffs_allege_possession_under_agree: The plaintiffs allege that they possess the property pursuant to an agreement.
predicates.reliefs_are_interconnected: The pleaded declaration and injunction claims are related to the same alleged agreement and possession.

issues.definition: When plaintiffs seeking rejection before trial plead an interconnected declaration and possession-based injunction arising from an agreement, the plaint is not rejected at the threshold merely because the declaration may not be maintainable.
